question:
A 51-year-old carpenter comes to the clinic reporting right shoulder pain with associated numbness
and weakness in his arm and hand. His symptoms began with intermittent tingling in his hand and have
progressed over 4 weeks to include worsening numbness, shoulder pain, and upper extremity
weakness. The pain is rated 6/10 at rest and intensifies with arm and hand movement. He has no prior
similar symptoms or trauma history, but believes it may be work-related. His medical history includes
well-controlled hypertension. Physical examination reveals decreased right grip strength (4/5), reduced
sensation in the medial palm, hypertonic and tender bilateral trapezius muscles, sternocleidomastoids,
and scalenes. The right first rib demonstrates rigidity and lack of movement during exhalation. Which
special test would most likely yield a positive result? Answer Choices: (A) Spurling test (B) Adson test
(C) Tinel's sign (D) Military brace test (E) Costoclavicular test (F) Upper limb tension test (G) Phalen's
test (H) Wright test (I) Allen test (J) Phalen test
 A. Phalen's test
B. Military brace test
C. Costoclavicular test
D. Upper limb tension test
E. Adson test
F. Tinel's sign
G. Spurling test
H. Wright test
I. Phalen test
J. Allen test
